title: Inhibition Kinetics Measurement
author: Tjusls China
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7y9hpz6
materials: Infinite M1000 Pro Automatic Microplate Reader

steps.title: Clean 96‑well plates
steps.instruction: Soak the plates in 75 % ethanol, place the container in an ultrasonic cleaner for 30 min to 1 h, wash the plates several times with ddH₂O, then dry them in an oven at 55 °C.

steps.title: Prepare inhibitor dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute each inhibitor in 100 % DMSO to a stock concentration of 8 mM (which yields 80 µM in the reaction), then prepare a 2‑fold serial dilution series covering 12 concentrations (use at least 8 different concentrations for the assay).

steps.title: Prepare enzyme solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the enzyme (protein) in its specific buffer to the standard concentration used for Km determination.

steps.title: Assemble reaction mixtures
steps.instruction:
In each well add 94 µL protein solution and 1 µL inhibitor solution (from the 2‑fold dilution series), incubate at room temperature for 5 min, then add 5 µL substrate CDC‑1. Prepare controls in parallel (three replicate wells each):
- Negative control: 94 µL protein solution, 1 µL DMSO, 5 µL substrate.
- Blank control: 94 µL protein buffer, 1 µL DMSO, 5 µL substrate.

steps.title: Program microplate reader
steps.instruction: In the Infinite M1000 Pro reader set the protocol to: shake 10 s at 654 rpm, then run a kinetic cycle that records fluorescence every cycle for 20 cycles (30 s per cycle).

steps.title: Run kinetic measurement
steps.instruction: Place the plate in the reader and start the program.

steps.title: Export and fit IC₅₀ data
steps.instruction: When the run finishes, save the data and import the 0‑200 s interval into GraphPad Prism. Perform a “nonlinear fit – straight line” to adjust the number of points used and obtain R². Subtract the blank baseline, then calculate inhibition % (Ir) for each well using Ir = (1 − Vr/V₀) × 100 %. Average Ir for each inhibitor concentration (Y) and plot against log[I] (X). Use “nonlinear fit – log(inhibitor) vs normalized response – variable slope” to obtain the IC₅₀ curve automatically.

steps.title: Assess reversible vs irreversible
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of protein concentrations around the screening value and a series of inhibitor concentrations around the IC₅₀ value. Plot V₀ versus [E] for each inhibitor level. Parallel straight lines indicate irreversible inhibition; lines intersecting at the origin indicate reversible inhibition.

steps.title: Determine inhibition type
steps.instruction:
Prepare substrate concentrations around the screening value and inhibitor concentrations around the IC₅₀ value. Generate a Lineweaver‑Burk plot (1/V₀ vs 1/[S]).
- Intersection at the Y‑axis → competitive inhibition.
- Intersection at the X‑axis → non‑competitive inhibition.
- Intersection elsewhere → mixed (including uncompetitive) inhibition.

steps.title: Calculate Ki
steps.instruction: After the inhibition mechanism is identified, calculate the inhibition constant Ki using the appropriate equation for the mechanism or by entering the IC₅₀ and assay conditions into the online converter at https://bioinfo-abcc.ncifcrf.gov/IC50_Ki_Converter/index.php.
